transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess things have just gotten out of hand at home. Ever since my father-in-law moved in, I’ve been… snapping at my wife over stupid little house stuff, things I wouldn’t normally make a big deal about.

And I’m letting things slide too—jobs around the house, paperwork, that kind of thing. I used to keep on top of it. I mean, I’m not working right now, so you’d think I’d have more time, right? But somehow it just piles up. Even when I go out to the workshop or try to fish—usually that clears my head—I can’t seem to quiet it down. My mind just keeps going.
Have you noticed that you’re not getting as much enjoyment out of things like working in the workshop or fishing as you used to?

I don’t know if I’d say I don’t enjoy them exactly. Like, I still go out there to the workshop and mess with things, or I’ll think about fishing, but… it’s hard to tell what’s the hobby and what’s just everything else getting in the way.

I mean, my father-in-law has all these little routines, and somehow the garage ends up involved—tools moved around, boxes where I had stuff laid out. Not that he means anything by it. He’s just… he’s particular. So I guess I haven’t really paid attention to whether it’s less enjoyable, or whether I’m just distracted when I try.
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest in things you used to really enjoy, like working in the workshop or going fishing?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I mean, I haven’t sat down and thought, “Do I still like fishing?” It’s more like I’ll get the gear together and then end up fussing with where something got put, or remembering some thing in the garage that’s out of place.

The workshop’s the same way. I still care about it, I think. I still like having my tools just so—my old neighbor used to joke I knew where every screw was, which… I probably did. But lately when I’m out there, my head’s not really on the project. So I don’t know if that’s losing interest or just not being able to settle into it.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the time, even when you're not dealing with the house or your father-in-law?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’m depressed most of the time, exactly. It’s more like I get wound up when I think about the house, or when something’s been moved, or there’s that whole routine going on.

When I’m away from it, I guess I haven’t really checked in with myself like that. I can be okay, or at least not thinking about it for a bit. Though even then, sometimes my mind circles back—like yesterday I was at the store and saw those little organizer bins, and then I started thinking about the garage shelves, and how my father-in-law stacked things in front of them. So… I’m not sure if that counts as feeling down, or just being irritated and preoccupied.
When you're away from home, like when you're out running errands or fishing, do you find yourself worrying about other things in life, not just what's happening at home?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way. Like if I’m out running errands, my mind does wander, sure, but it’ll be something stupid like whether I remembered to get the right size screws, or I’ll see a display at the hardware store and think, “Oh, that’d fit on the shelf,” and then that takes me back to the garage.

Fishing, I don’t know. I haven’t really been able to make it a whole separate thing in my head lately. I’ll be standing there by the water and start thinking about how my tackle box used to be organized, and then I’m back to thinking about the house again. So… other things in life? I guess I haven’t noticed much besides that same stuff looping back around.

Do you find yourself worrying a lot about things outside of the house situation, like work, your health, or other responsibilities, even when you’re not thinking about the garage or your father-in-law?

I’m not sure, honestly. Work isn’t really a thing for me right now, so I don’t know if that counts. Health… I mean, I’ll think about it if something aches, but then—well, like last week I was looking for the heating pad and ended up finding this old coffee can full of bolts I’d been meaning to sort, and that kind of took over my head for a while.

Responsibilities, yeah, I guess everybody worries about those some. Bills, errands, whether I forgot something at the store. But it doesn’t feel like I’m sitting around worrying about everything under the sun. It usually circles back to the house stuff somehow, or I just get distracted by something connected to it. So… I don’t know if I’d say “a lot” outside of that.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried even about things that aren’t related to the house or your father-in-law, like relationships, your future, or other everyday problems?

I don’t really know. Relationships, future… those sound kind of big, and I guess if you ask anybody they’d say they think about them sometimes.

For me, it’s hard to separate it out. Like I’ll start thinking, “What’s this place going to look like in five years,” but then I’m picturing the garage, or all the stuff that got put where it doesn’t belong, and then I’m not really thinking about the future in some general way anymore. I’m thinking about that.

Everyday problems, sure, I get annoyed or worried a little, like if I forgot to do something, but I haven’t noticed myself worrying about everything like that. It mostly just kind of drifts back to the same home stuff.

Do you find yourself having repeated, intrusive thoughts about certain things—like needing things to be in a specific order or worrying that something bad will happen if they aren’t—and do you feel driven to do something to ease that worry, like checking, organizing, or arranging things?

I don’t know if I’d call it intrusive exactly. I mean, I like things where they belong, especially in the garage, because if you’re looking for a wrench and it’s not on the peg where it’s supposed to be, then you waste twenty minutes, and then you forget what you were even doing.

But “something bad will happen”… I don’t think it’s like that. It’s more just irritating, or it gets under my skin. Like I’ll straighten something or move it back, but then I might notice the shelf is dusty, and then I’m thinking about how I used to keep extra jars up there, and it kind of becomes this whole thing.

I’m not sure I’m answering right. I don’t feel like I have some ritual I have to do, if that’s what you mean. It’s just hard to let some of that stuff sit wrong.

Do you ever feel really bothered or upset by thoughts that keep coming into your mind, even if you try not to have them—like needing things to be just right or worrying something will go wrong if they aren’t?

I’m not sure. I mean, I do get bothered when stuff isn’t where it should be, but I don’t know that it’s some thought barging in that I can’t stop, exactly.

Like, if I see something out of place, yeah, it can stick in my head. But then sometimes I’ll start thinking about the shelf it’s on, or how I should’ve fixed that hinge months ago, and then I’m off thinking about whether I still have the right screws somewhere. So it’s hard for me to say it’s one specific thought.

I don’t really sit there thinking, “If this isn’t just right, something terrible will happen.” It’s more like… it nags at me, I guess. Gets under my skin. But I don’t know if that’s what you mean.

Do these thoughts about things being out of place or needing to be just right ever become so bothersome that they interfere with what you’re trying to do—like stopping you from focusing, making you late, or keeping you from doing something you need to do?

Yeah… I mean, I guess it has interfered. I don’t like saying that, but it has.

It’s not always like I’m standing there lining things up for hours, but I’ll get stuck on something being wrong or out of place, and then the thing I was supposed to be doing just doesn’t get done. I missed an important filing date for my contractor license, which… that still makes me feel stupid, because I used to stay on top of that kind of thing. And I’ve had to turn down or push off some small repair jobs because I’m just not keeping up the way I used to.

And at home, it’s caused tension. My wife gets frustrated, and I get defensive, and then something that should be simple turns into a whole thing. I’m not following through on family stuff the way I should. So… yes, it’s gotten in the way.
